title: Singleton List
body:
A list with a single Node

It is worth its own name because it is one of the two cases every list function gets wrong.
The empty list is the other.

```c++
Node* head = new Node;
head->data = 7;
head->next = NULL;      // head is both the first node and the last
```

The trap: in a singleton, `head` and the tail are the same [[Node]], so deleting the only
element has to set `head` back to `NULL` rather than just unlinking. Code that walks with
`while (cur->next != NULL)` to find the last node quietly does nothing here, which is
usually correct by accident and worth checking rather than trusting.

Test every list operation on three inputs: empty, singleton, and three or more. A [[Driver]]
that only tries the third one passes and proves nothing.
